title: SKY GATEWAY HYDERABAD — weekly quiz bank
note: Original questions aligned to PMBOK® Guide 8th Edition topics; scenario numbers are simulated.
derivedFrom: mission brief §5.2/§6 weekly topics — replace with the official outline

questions.q: Which of these is a PROJECT rather than an operation at Hyderabad Airport?
options: Extending the runway from about 2,133 m to about 3,505 m
Daily runway friction and FOD inspections
questions.explanation: A project is temporary and creates a unique result; the extension has a start, an end and a unique deliverable. The others are repetitive, ongoing operations.

wrongExplanations.1: Payroll is an ongoing business process.
wrongExplanations.2: Inspections repeat every day indefinitely — that is operations.

questions.q: In the simulator the runway, terminal, tower and landside projects are managed together to deliver the "revived gateway" benefits. That coordinated group is best called a:
questions.explanation: A programme is a group of related projects (and activities) managed in a coordinated way to obtain benefits not available from managing them individually.

questions.q: A portfolio is best defined as:
options: A group of tasks that share one resource
The set of deliverables of a single project
Projects, programmes and operations managed as a group to achieve strategic objectives
questions.explanation: Portfolios are aligned to strategy; their components need not be related to each other.

questions.q: Which of the following is an ORGANISATIONAL PROCESS ASSET (OPA) for the Hyderabad programme?
options: The PMO's lessons-learned repository from an earlier airport project
The exchange rate of the rupee
questions.explanation: OPAs are internal plans, processes, policies and knowledge bases. Climate, law and exchange rates are enterprise environmental factors (EEFs).

questions.q: The July–September monsoon in Sindh is an enterprise environmental factor (EEF) for this project.
questions.explanation: EEFs are conditions not under the team's control that influence the project — climate is a classic external EEF.

questions.q: Which type of PMO takes direct control of projects by managing them itself?
questions.explanation: Supportive PMOs provide templates and training (low control), controlling PMOs require compliance (moderate), directive PMOs manage the projects (high control).

questions.q: Which statement best describes the role of the project manager?
options: The person who funds the project and owns the business case
The regulator who certifies the aerodrome
The person assigned by the performing organisation to lead the team responsible for achieving the project objectives
The head of the engineering department
questions.explanation: The sponsor funds and champions; functional managers run departments; the project manager leads the project team to achieve the objectives.

questions.q: Because projects are temporary, the deliverables they create must also be temporary.
questions.explanation: The project is temporary; its outputs (a runway, a terminal) may last for decades.

questions.q: The PMBOK® Guide is best described as:
options: A standard and body of knowledge describing principles, performance domains and practices, to be tailored
A step-by-step methodology that must be followed exactly
questions.explanation: PMBOK is a framework and standard, not a methodology. Teams tailor it to the context.

questions.q: Which characteristic is typical of a PREDICTIVE life cycle?
options: Requirements are elaborated every two weeks
Scope, time and cost are determined early and changes are carefully managed
The product is released continuously from day one
questions.explanation: Predictive (waterfall) life cycles plan most of the work up front — appropriate for runway pavements where change is expensive.

questions.q: The five focus areas (process groups) used in PMBOK 8 are Initiating, Planning, Executing, Closing and:
questions.explanation: Monitoring and Controlling runs in parallel with the other focus areas throughout the project.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a phase gate such as G1 at the end of planning?
options: To freeze all change for the rest of the project
A go / no-go decision on continuing to the next phase, based on defined criteria
questions.explanation: Gates (kill points) review performance and readiness and decide whether to continue, change or stop.

questions.q: Process groups (focus areas) are the same thing as project phases.
questions.explanation: Phases divide the life cycle over time (design, build, commission); focus areas can all occur within one phase.

questions.q: Which activity belongs to the INITIATING focus area?
options: Developing the project charter and identifying stakeholders
questions.explanation: Initiating defines a new project or phase and obtains authorisation: charter and stakeholder identification.

questions.q: The project team links the runway extension directly to diversion and regional-route benefits in every gate review. This best reflects the principle of:
questions.explanation: Value focus means continually checking that outputs deliver the intended outcomes and benefits.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a PMBOK performance domain?
questions.explanation: Performance domains are groups of related activities critical to delivering outcomes (e.g., stakeholders, schedule, risk). Concrete batching is a construction activity.

questions.q: Tailoring means:
options: Copying the previous project plan unchanged
Adapting the approach, governance and processes to suit the project's context
questions.explanation: Tailoring selects and adjusts practices to the size, risk, complexity and culture of the project.

questions.q: Monitoring and controlling only happens at the end of each phase.
questions.explanation: Monitoring and controlling is continuous: performance is measured against baselines throughout.

questions.q: Which are the three accountabilities in Scrum?
options: Team lead, QA lead, Release manager
questions.explanation: Scrum defines exactly three accountabilities within one Scrum Team.

questions.q: Who is accountable for ordering the product backlog for the terminal IT stream?
questions.explanation: The Product Owner maximises value by ordering the product backlog.

questions.q: The terminal IT team's last four velocities were 21, 24, 18 and 25 story points. About how many sprints are needed for 132 remaining points?
questions.explanation: Average velocity = (21 + 24 + 18 + 25) ÷ 4 = 22. Sprints = 132 ÷ 22 = 6.

questions.q: Why does a Kanban board set work-in-progress (WIP) limits?
options: To improve flow and expose bottlenecks
To make sure everyone is always busy
questions.explanation: Limiting WIP reduces multitasking and queues, so cycle time falls and bottlenecks become visible.

questions.q: In Scrum the team should change the sprint length each sprint to fit the work.
questions.explanation: Sprints keep a consistent length to create a predictable cadence.

questions.q: For the Hyderabad programme, which delivery approach best fits?
options: Hybrid: predictive for pavements and steel, Agile for terminal IT
Pure predictive for everything, including software
Pure Scrum for everything, including the runway
questions.explanation: Choose per deliverable: certain, costly-to-change civil works suit predictive; uncertain software suits Agile.

questions.q: Which is the most appropriate use of an AI assistant such as MEHRAN?
options: Signing contracts on behalf of the sponsor
Approving change requests without human review
Drafting risk-register entries from meeting notes for a human to review
questions.explanation: AI augments the PM: it drafts, analyses and explains; humans stay accountable for decisions (human in the loop).

questions.q: Using Little's law, a Kanban board holds 12 items in progress with a throughput of 3 items per day. What is the average cycle time in days?
questions.explanation: Cycle time = WIP ÷ throughput = 12 ÷ 3 = 4 days.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the sprint REVIEW?
options: Inspect how the team worked and improve its process
Plan the work of the next sprint only
Inspect the increment with stakeholders and adapt the product backlog
questions.explanation: The review inspects the product; the retrospective inspects the process.

questions.q: The scope baseline consists of:
options: The approved scope statement, WBS and WBS dictionary
The charter and the business case
questions.explanation: These three items, approved, form the scope baseline that change control protects.

questions.q: The "100 % rule" of the WBS states that:
options: Each package must cost the same
The WBS includes all of the work and only the work of the project
Every package must be 100 % complete before the next starts
questions.explanation: Child elements sum to exactly the parent — nothing missing, nothing extra.

questions.q: The lowest level of the WBS, where cost and duration can be estimated and managed, is the:
questions.explanation: Work packages are decomposed into activities for scheduling; control accounts group work packages for EVM.

questions.q: Gold plating (adding features the customer did not request) is good practice because the customer will be pleased.
questions.explanation: Gold plating adds cost and risk outside the approved scope; deliver what was agreed, and propose extras through change control.

questions.q: What is the difference between VALIDATE SCOPE and CONTROL QUALITY?
options: Control quality checks correctness; validate scope obtains the customer's formal acceptance
Control quality is done by the customer
questions.explanation: Deliverables are usually verified (control quality) first, then accepted by the customer (validate scope).

questions.q: Which tool links each requirement (e.g., "Code E capable apron stand") to its source, WBS element and test?
questions.explanation: The RTM traces requirements from origin through deliverables to verification.

questions.q: An official asks for a VIP lounge, and the contractor adds it without a change request. This is:
questions.explanation: Uncontrolled additions to scope without adjusting time, cost and resources are scope creep.

questions.q: WBS 3 (runway) has eight work packages budgeted at PKR 2.4, 1.8, 2.2, 3.1, 1.5, 0.9, 0.6 and 0.5 bn. What is the budget of WBS 3 in PKR bn?
"A runway 3,505 m long and 45 m wide with 7.5 m shoulders" describes:
questions.explanation: Product scope = features and functions of the result; project scope = the work needed to deliver it.

questions.q: Extension earthworks (3.2) have estimates O = 40, M = 55, P = 88 days. What is the PERT expected duration?
For the same activity (O = 40, P = 88), what is the PERT standard deviation?
A (5 days) precedes B (8) and C (10); B and C both precede D (4). All links are finish-to-start. What is the project duration?
questions.explanation: Paths: A-B-D = 17, A-C-D = 19. The longest path (critical path) is 19 days.

questions.q: In the same network, what is the total float of activity B?
questions.explanation: B is on the 17-day path; 19 − 17 = 2 days of float.

questions.q: When crashing, which activity should be shortened first?
options: The activity with the highest cost slope
The longest activity in the project
The critical activity with the lowest cost slope
questions.explanation: Only critical activities shorten the project; choose the cheapest per day first, and re-check the critical path after each step.

questions.q: The apron slab normally takes 30 days for PKR 60 m; crashed it takes 24 days for PKR 84 m. What is the cost slope in PKR million per day?
questions.explanation: Cost slope = (84 − 60) ÷ (30 − 24) = 24 ÷ 6 = 4 PKR million per day.

questions.q: Starting terminal fit-out in zones where glazing is complete, instead of waiting for all glazing, is an example of:
questions.explanation: Fast-tracking overlaps activities normally done in sequence; it adds risk rather than direct cost.

questions.q: The British Columbia Transportation case is discussed with scheduling. For seasonal civil works such as paving, which practice best handles weather windows?
options: Use the same productivity rate all year
Schedule paving only after all other work is finished
Model seasonal work calendars and constraints explicitly in the schedule
Ignore weather and add a single contingency at the end
questions.explanation: Calendars and constraints make weather windows visible to CPM, so float and risk are realistic.

questions.q: In a schedule with no imposed finish date, critical-path activities have zero total float.
questions.explanation: By definition the critical path is the longest path, with zero float when the late finish equals the early finish.

questions.q: The critical path has a PERT mean of 300 days and σ = 10 days. To the nearest per cent, what is the probability of finishing within 310 days?
What is the correct order for integrated change control?
options: Log the request → analyse impact → CCB decision → update baselines → communicate
questions.explanation: Impact analysis comes before the decision; approved changes update plans and are communicated.

questions.q: Who approves changes to the performance measurement baseline, per a typical change management plan?
questions.explanation: The CCB (or the authority defined in the change management plan) approves baseline changes.

questions.q: At week 40, EV = PKR 4.2 bn and PV = PKR 4.8 bn. What is the schedule variance in PKR bn?
questions.explanation: SV = EV − PV = 4.2 − 4.8 = −0.6 bn (behind schedule).

questions.q: With EV = 4.2 bn and PV = 4.8 bn, what is the SPI (three decimals)?
A change request is only needed for changes that increase cost.
questions.explanation: Any change to approved baselines (scope, schedule, cost) — or to controlled documents — goes through change control, whichever direction.

questions.q: SPI has fallen to 0.88 against a control threshold of 0.90. What should the PM do first?
options: Analyse the root cause and propose corrective action through change control
questions.explanation: Breaching a variance threshold triggers analysis and, where baselines are affected, a change request.

questions.q: Closing a PHASE includes:
options: Confirming acceptance of the phase deliverables, recording lessons and archiving records
questions.explanation: Phase closure formally completes the phase so the next can start with what was learned.

questions.q: A storm has flooded the subgrade today. Where is this recorded and managed?
options: Only in the risk register as a future uncertainty
In the issue log — it is a current problem
questions.explanation: Risks are future uncertainties; when they happen they become issues to resolve (and the risk register is updated).

questions.q: What does configuration management control?
options: Versions and characteristics of deliverables and documents, such as drawings
questions.explanation: Configuration management ensures everyone builds from the current approved drawing revision.

questions.q: Training paving crews before work starts is which cost-of-quality category?
questions.explanation: Prevention costs avoid defects; appraisal costs find them; failure costs fix them.

questions.q: Cube strengths average 40 MPa with σ = 1.5 MPa. What is the upper control limit at ±3σ?
questions.explanation: UCL = mean + 3σ = 40 + 4.5 = 44.5 MPa.

questions.q: On a control chart, seven consecutive points on one side of the mean indicate:
options: A possible special (assignable) cause to investigate
The process is perfectly in control
questions.explanation: The "rule of seven" is a run signalling a non-random shift.

questions.q: A Pareto chart of runway defects is used to:
options: Focus on the few causes producing most of the defects
questions.explanation: Pareto (80/20) ranks categories by frequency so effort goes to the vital few.

questions.q: Quality costs (PKR m): prevention 20, appraisal 35, internal failure 60, external failure 15. What is the cost of CONFORMANCE?
questions.explanation: Conformance = prevention + appraisal = 20 + 35 = 55. Non-conformance = 60 + 15 = 75.

questions.q: Control limits and specification limits are the same thing.
questions.explanation: Control limits come from process data (voice of the process); specification limits come from requirements (voice of the customer).

questions.q: A basic fit-out that meets every requirement without defects is:
options: Neither — grade and quality are the same
questions.explanation: Grade is a category of features; quality is the degree to which requirements are met.

questions.q: To find why concrete cubes failed, the team brainstorms causes under Materials, Methods, Machines, People, Environment and Measurement. Which tool is this?
questions.explanation: The fishbone groups potential root causes by category.

questions.q: Of 120 concrete cubes tested, 6 failed. What percentage failed?
Mid-term: AGL cabling has O = 10, M = 16, P = 28 days. What is the PERT expected duration?
Mid-term: EV = PKR 9 bn and AC = PKR 10 bn. What is the CPI?
questions.explanation: CPI = EV ÷ AC = 9 ÷ 10 = 0.9 — each rupee spent earns 90 paisa of value.

questions.q: Mid-term: what distinguishes a programme from a portfolio?
options: Programme components are related and managed for shared benefits; portfolio components serve strategy and may be unrelated
questions.explanation: Programmes coordinate related work for benefits; portfolios select and balance work for strategic objectives.

questions.q: Mid-term: in which Scrum event does the team inspect its own way of working?
questions.explanation: The retrospective plans improvements to quality and effectiveness.

questions.q: Mid-term: which is found in the WBS dictionary?
options: The project budget at completion only
Description, deliverables, acceptance criteria and owner of each WBS element
questions.explanation: The dictionary details each element of the WBS.

questions.q: Mid-term: an activity has ES = day 12 and LS = day 18. What is its total float?
questions.explanation: Total float = LS − ES = 18 − 12 = 6 days.

questions.q: Mid-term: fast-tracking always increases the project's direct cost.
questions.explanation: Fast-tracking mainly increases risk (rework); crashing is the technique that adds cost.

questions.q: Mid-term: the regulator mandates a longer RESA. How is this handled?
options: Through integrated change control — mandatory changes still update baselines formally
questions.explanation: Mandatory changes skip the "whether" debate but not the documentation, impact analysis and baseline update.

questions.q: Mid-term: which observation on a control chart is a clear signal of a special cause?
options: All points inside the limits with no pattern
Points alternating randomly around the mean
A point beyond the upper control limit
questions.explanation: Points outside the ±3σ limits indicate an assignable cause.

questions.q: BAC = PKR 48 bn, EV = 18 bn, AC = 20 bn. Assuming the current CPI continues, what is the EAC in PKR bn (two decimals)?
Same data (BAC 48, EV 18, AC 20). What is the TCPI to finish on the original BAC (two decimals)?
questions.explanation: TCPI = (BAC − EV) ÷ (BAC − AC) = 30 ÷ 28 = 1.07.

questions.q: Same data. What is the VAC (PKR bn, two decimals)?
questions.explanation: VAC = BAC − EAC = 48 − 53.33 = −5.33 bn (forecast overrun).

questions.q: Same data. What is the ETC in PKR bn (two decimals)?
The contingency reserve is intended for:
options: Identified risks (known-unknowns) and is part of the cost baseline
Unknown-unknowns and is outside the cost baseline
questions.explanation: Management reserve covers unknown-unknowns and sits outside the baseline but inside the budget.

questions.q: Project budget = ?
questions.explanation: Work packages + contingency = cost baseline; + management reserve = project budget.

questions.q: Estimating the terminal at PKR 210,000 per m² of floor area is:
questions.explanation: Parametric estimating uses a statistical relationship between a parameter (m²) and cost.

questions.q: Using PKR 210,000 per m², what is the parametric estimate for an 18,000 m² terminal, in PKR bn?
Funding-limit reconciliation can require rescheduling work so spending stays within annual funding limits.
questions.explanation: If planned spend exceeds the year's limit, work is re-sequenced (or funds re-negotiated).

questions.q: A flash flood has a 30 % probability and a PKR 300 m impact. What is its EMV magnitude in PKR m?
questions.explanation: EMV = P × I = 0.30 × 300 = 90 (a threat, so −90).

questions.q: Without pumps: 30 % chance of a PKR 300 m loss. Pumps cost PKR 40 m and cut the probability to 10 %. By how much (PKR m) do pumps reduce the expected cost?
A risk is rated probability 4 and impact 5 on 1–5 scales. What is its P × I score?
questions.explanation: 4 × 5 = 20 — in the red zone of a 5×5 matrix.

questions.q: Buying contractor's all-risk insurance against flood damage is which threat response?
questions.explanation: Transfer shifts the impact (and ownership of the response) to a third party, at a premium.

questions.q: Adding capacity so the solar plant can sell surplus power is which opportunity response?
questions.explanation: Enhance increases the probability or impact of an opportunity; exploit makes it certain; share partners with a third party.

questions.q: In the pandemic-vaccine case (AstraZeneca) studied in Week 10, manufacturing doses "at risk" in parallel with clinical trials is best described as:
options: Accepting financial risk to compress the schedule by overlapping phases
questions.explanation: Overlapping normally sequential work (fast-tracking) trades a known financial exposure for time when the value of time is very high.

questions.q: A risk that arises as a direct result of implementing a risk response is a:
questions.explanation: Residual risk remains after the response; a secondary risk is created by the response itself.

questions.q: Risks only need to be reviewed at gate meetings.
questions.explanation: Risk monitoring is continuous: triggers, new risks, and response effectiveness are tracked throughout.

questions.q: A Monte Carlo simulation gives P80 = 1,020 days. This means:
options: The project will take exactly 1,020 days
There is an 80 % probability of finishing in 1,020 days or less
There is an 80 % chance of being late
questions.explanation: P80 is the 80th percentile of the simulated finish distribution.

questions.q: Three risks: a threat 20 % × PKR 500 m, a threat 50 % × PKR 80 m, and an opportunity 40 % × PKR 150 m. What is the NET threat exposure in PKR m?
questions.explanation: Threats: 100 + 40 = 140. Opportunity: 60. Net = 140 − 60 = 80.

questions.q: Under a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract, cost-overrun risk lies mainly with:
questions.explanation: The seller must deliver at the agreed price; the buyer needs well-defined scope.

questions.q: When scope is highly uncertain (e.g., early IT integration), which contract type is most suitable?
options: Lump sum with no change clause
questions.explanation: Cost-reimbursable contracts suit uncertain scope; the buyer carries more cost risk.

questions.q: Weights: price 40 %, technical 30 %, experience 20 %, schedule 10 %. A bidder scores 8, 7, 9 and 6 (out of 10). What is the weighted score?
FPIF: target cost PKR 100 m, target fee 10 m, buyer/seller share 80/20, ceiling 120 m. Actual cost is 90 m. What is the final price in PKR m?
questions.explanation: Underrun = 10; seller keeps 20 % = 2, so fee = 12. Price = 90 + 12 = 102 (below the ceiling).

questions.q: Renting a crane costs PKR 1.2 m/day. Buying costs PKR 90 m plus PKR 0.3 m/day to operate. After how many days does buying break even?
The purpose of a bidder conference is to:
options: Give all prospective sellers the same information at the same time
Negotiate a price with the favourite bidder
questions.explanation: Equal access to information keeps the competition fair.

questions.q: During an active bid evaluation it is acceptable to accept a bidder's hospitality as long as nobody finds out.
questions.explanation: Conflicts of interest must be avoided and disclosed; professional responsibility requires refusing and reporting.

questions.q: The procurement statement of work (SOW) describes:
options: The item to be procured in enough detail for sellers to decide whether they can provide it
questions.explanation: The SOW is the scope for that procurement.

questions.q: A contractor submits a claim for extra costs caused by a disputed design change. The preferred first step is:
options: Negotiation under the contract's claims-administration procedure
questions.explanation: Negotiation first; alternative dispute resolution (mediation, arbitration) before courts.

questions.q: How many communication channels exist among 15 stakeholders?
The core team grows from 10 to 14 people. By how many do the communication channels increase?
questions.explanation: 10 people: 45 channels; 14 people: 91 channels; increase = 46.

questions.q: A provincial secretary has high power but low interest in day-to-day progress. The strategy is to:
questions.explanation: Power/interest grid: high/high manage closely; high power/low interest keep satisfied; low/high keep informed; low/low monitor.

questions.q: The civil and MEP leads argue in every meeting about responsibilities. In Tuckman's model the team is in:
questions.explanation: Storming is the conflict stage as roles and working styles are contested.

questions.q: Which conflict-resolution mode generally produces the most lasting result?
questions.explanation: Collaboration addresses root causes and builds commitment (win-win).

questions.q: In a RACI matrix, how many people should be Accountable for a deliverable?
questions.explanation: One "A" per deliverable avoids confusion; several people can be Responsible.

questions.q: Resource levelling differs from resource smoothing because levelling:
options: May change the critical path and end date to respect resource limits
questions.explanation: Smoothing works within float; levelling can extend the project.

questions.q: The salience model classifies stakeholders by power, legitimacy and urgency.
questions.explanation: Stakeholders with all three attributes are "definitive" and need the most attention.

questions.q: In Herzberg's theory, which is a HYGIENE factor?
options: Salary and working conditions (e.g., heat shelters)
questions.explanation: Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction; motivators (recognition, achievement, growth) create satisfaction.

questions.q: Stakeholders consult a live project dashboard whenever they choose. This is:
questions.explanation: Pull: recipients access information at their discretion. Push: sent to recipients. Interactive: real-time exchange.

questions.q: A start-to-start (SS) dependency means:
options: The successor cannot start until the predecessor starts
The successor must finish before the predecessor starts
The successor cannot start until the predecessor finishes
questions.explanation: SS links starts — e.g., markings can start once surfacing has started, with a lag.

questions.q: A finish-to-start link has a 5-day lag. The predecessor finishes at the end of day 20. On which day can the successor start at the earliest?
questions.explanation: Successor ES = predecessor EF + lag = 20 + 5 = 25 (in end-of-day day numbering).

questions.q: On an effort-driven, fixed-work task, assigning a second identical crew will:
questions.explanation: Work = duration × units; with fixed work, more units reduce duration.

questions.q: After saving a baseline, which view compares current dates against it?
questions.explanation: The Tracking Gantt shows baseline bars beneath current bars.

questions.q: A milestone such as "G2 — Runway ready for overlay" has a duration of:
questions.explanation: Milestones mark points in time; they consume no time.

questions.q: A negative lag (lead) allows a successor to start before its predecessor finishes.
questions.explanation: Leads overlap linked activities — a form of fast-tracking.

questions.q: A red over-allocation indicator appears on the paving crew. The usual remedy in the tool is:
questions.explanation: Levelling delays or splits tasks so demand stays within capacity.

questions.q: Three engineers are assigned full-time to a 10-day task with 8-hour days. How many hours of work is this?
questions.explanation: Work = 10 days × 8 h × 3 = 240 hours.

questions.q: Which file format does this simulator export so the schedule opens in MS Project?
questions.explanation: MS Project reads the Microsoft Project Data Interchange (XML) format; CSV is also offered.

questions.q: A monthly status report to the sponsor should lead with:
options: A full list of every task
Progress against baseline, forecast (EAC, finish date), top risks and decisions needed
questions.explanation: Executives need performance, forecast, exceptions and decisions.

questions.q: Presenting to the provincial cabinet, you should tailor the message by:
options: Starting with benefits and decisions needed, then the evidence
questions.explanation: Tailor to audience: executives want the "so what" first.

questions.q: Which visual best shows schedule slippage to a non-specialist audience?
options: A Gantt chart with baseline bars beneath current bars
questions.explanation: Baseline vs current bars make slippage visible at a glance.

questions.q: You must report a 40-day delay. Best practice is to:
options: Report early, explain causes, and present options with impacts
questions.explanation: Bad news early, with options, preserves trust and decision time.

questions.q: A good project dashboard displays every metric the system can calculate.
questions.explanation: Dashboards should show the few indicators that drive decisions, with thresholds.

questions.q: In a two-minute project pitch, which element matters most?
options: The value: the problem, the benefits and why now
questions.explanation: Lead with value and outcomes.

questions.q: A slide says SPI = 0.9 and PV = PKR 10 bn. What EV (PKR bn) should the chart show?
questions.explanation: EV = SPI × PV = 0.9 × 10 = 9 bn.

questions.q: An AMBER status (RAG) usually means:
options: At risk, but recoverable with management action
questions.explanation: Green on track; amber at risk with action; red off track needing escalation.

questions.q: An examiner asks a question you cannot answer during your presentation. The best response is to:
options: Acknowledge it, give what you know, and commit to follow up
questions.explanation: Honesty and follow-up maintain credibility.

questions.q: Which sequence best describes closing the project?
options: Confirm acceptance → transfer deliverables → close procurements → lessons learned → archive → release resources
questions.explanation: Closure formalises acceptance, transfers ownership and captures knowledge before the team disperses.

questions.q: When are most benefits of the revived airport realised?
options: After the project closes, during operations
questions.explanation: Benefits (movements, passengers, on-time performance) accrue in operations and are tracked by the benefits owner.

questions.q: Final review: at completion BAC = EV = PKR 50 bn and AC = 54 bn. What is the final CPI (two decimals)?
Final review: how many communication channels exist among 8 people?
Final review: O = 6, M = 9, P = 18 days. What is the PERT expected duration?
Lessons learned should be collected only at the end of the project.
questions.explanation: They are captured throughout and consolidated at closure into the organisational process assets.

questions.q: Before administrative closure, a procurement audit is performed to:
options: Review the procurement process for lessons and compliance
questions.explanation: The audit examines the whole procurement process so the organisation learns from it.

questions.q: ORAT (operational readiness and airport transfer) mainly ensures that:
options: People, processes and systems are ready to operate the new facility from day one
questions.explanation: ORAT trials, training and procedures turn outputs into working operations.

questions.q: The final project report typically includes:
options: The first draft of the charter
Summary of scope, quality, cost and schedule performance against objectives, plus benefits status
questions.explanation: It records how the project performed against its success criteria.

questions.q: Final review: a threat has a 25 % probability and a PKR 400 m impact. What is its EMV magnitude in PKR m?
